sections.heading: Identity
sections.content: Aetheris is a shattered high-fantasy continent of war-torn ruins, scavengers, warbands, zealots and conspiracies. Five great factions contend over the twelve shards of the Ethereal Crystal. Power takes a price in memory, name, blood or sanity. Its Cycle of Aetherfalls has ended: in the present, **no reset happens during play**.

sections.heading: Geography
sections.content: The Hollow Marches occupy the contested centre, with Hollow Refuge as a neutral starting settlement. [The Radiant Ascendancy](/player/e/REG-002) lies north; [the Tyrant's Dominion](/player/e/REG-003) east; [the Fractured Nexus](/player/e/REG-004) north-west; [the Eternal Veil](/player/e/REG-005) west by the Black Tides; and [the Verdant Rebirth](/player/e/REG-006) south.

sections.heading: Five dominions and ruling factions
sections.content:
| Dominion | Faction | Capital | Chief fortress |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [Radiant Ascendancy](/player/e/REG-002) | Celestial Order | Empyrean Spire | Golden Aerie |
| [Tyrant's Dominion](/player/e/REG-003) | Crimson Legion | Varkhaal | Red Bastion |
| [Fractured Nexus](/player/e/REG-004) | Arcane Consortium | Zepharyos | Nexus Collegium |
| [Eternal Veil](/player/e/REG-005) | Shadow Pact | Noctis | Nightglass |
| [Verdant Rebirth](/player/e/REG-006) | Wildborn Clans | Rootspire | Verdant Crown |

All five coexist. Rival enclaves operate inside each dominion. The bibles distinguish the capitals named by the story cards from the nearby chief fortresses supplied by the tabletop books.

sections.heading: At campaign start
sections.content: The Cycle ended about thirty years before the current Year 31 Unbound. History accumulates; the five dominions no longer take turns replacing one another. The Hollow Marches stay contested; the first regular ships cross from the Eternal Veil to Kaelmar.

sections.heading: Calendar structure
sections.content:
A single **363-day** year is used on both continents. There are twelve 30-day months grouped into four seasons, plus three festival days outside the months. Weeks have seven days.

| Season | Month 1 | Month 2 | Month 3 | Festival and placement |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Spring | Spring Dawn | First Seed | Monsoon | Spring Equinox: before Spring Dawn 1; New Year's Day |
| Summer | Midnight Sun | Dry Wind | Harvest | Midsummer: Midnight Sun 15; **not** an extra day |
| Autumn | Fall | Last Seed | Old Winds | Autumn Equinox: before Fall 1 |
| Winter | Snowfall | Evernight | Winter's Dusk | Evernight Festival: between Evernight 30 and Winter's Dusk 1 |

The three extra days are Spring Equinox, Autumn Equinox and Evernight Festival. Midsummer occurs within an existing month and does not increase the year to 364 days.

sections.heading: Date naming
sections.content: Example: `Midnight Sun 15, 300 AB`. Kaelmar counts After Bloom (AB). Aetheris counts Unbound years from the broken Cycle: **300 AB is Year 31 Unbound**, and the stated conversion is Unbound = AB − 269.

sections.heading: Established nature

sections.heading: Overview
sections.content: Kaelholm is the renamed Kaelith-East, the enclave that kept Kaelith's name, archives, scholar corps and tribunals. It is the largest city on Kaelmar and the first port for ships arriving from Aetheris.

sections.heading: Authority and methods
sections.content: The Kaelholm power is led in 300 AB by [Archivist-Elder Venn Tull](/player/e/NPC-308). It wants every vault catalogued and the change turned back. Its tribunals can punish a person by scraping their name from every roll, a practice called being "burned".

sections.heading: Current conditions
sections.content: The first regular ships from Aetheris are arriving. Kaelholm wants to be first to examine any surviving guardian or old vault. City wards, population, port name and exact internal geography are UNDEFINED.

sections.heading: Identity
sections.content: Kaelmar is a post-collapse fantasy continent, three hundred years after the Shrouding. Kaelith's Great Work attempted to move minds between bodies and conquer death. Its failure joined spellwork, flesh and forest. Failsafes paused the transformation; the Bloom grew through the ruins. The setting's central conflict asks who may choose what shape another life takes.

sections.heading: Factions and pressures
sections.content: Kaelholm wants the old works catalogued. The Spore Circle tends the Bloom and its Eastern Tendril burns Kaelith work. The Continuity watches the old web. The Convergence Collective advocates voluntary completion of the change, while the Ascendancy wants rule by a chosen few. In Ashvale, Boundary Keepers, Bloom-Speakers and Wrights disagree on how to keep their town safe.

sections.heading: Magic and supernatural conditions
sections.content: Kaelith glyph-work and [the Bloom](/player/e/COS-301) express a common grammar of call and answer. Their cost is blood, memory or self. The glass exists in limited seeps. Under-roads and root paths reach the Ethereal Realm's border layer.

sections.heading: Common speech
sections.content:
Common (Aetheris) and Kaelish (Kaelmar) are distant cousin languages. At the table, they may be treated as one language unless the GM deliberately wants the barrier to matter in an adventure. This is the stated flexible convention in the setting bible, not a claim that the languages are identical in-world.

Sailors across the Black Tides mix Common and Kaelish in a trade pidgin called **Tidecant**.

sections.heading: Local speech and scripts
sections.content:
| Name | Established use | Rules mapping from source |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Veilspeech | Shadow Pact cant | Thieves' Cant |
| Root-tongue | Wildborn language | Druidic for druids, Sylvan for others |
| The First Grammar | Kaelith's dead writing system, read but never spoken | Rare language |
| Circle-tongue | Spore Circle language used during communion | No mapping given |

Standard D&D 5.5e languages also exist on both continents. Exact translation rules for mixed-language encounters remain a table choice.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.content:
A sunless sea between Aetheris and Kaelmar.

- **On the Aetheris side** it is one of the Eternal Veil's sites. (A: Geography)
- **On the Kaelmar side** it lies beyond Kaelholm. (K: Geography)

sections.heading: Established lore
sections.content:
- **Why it is dark.** The Rift's trench runs beneath it, which is why it is sunless.
- **The crossing.** Ships run between [Kaelholm](/player/e/SET-302) and the ports of the Eternal Veil. The crossing takes about two weeks in the dark, and the crew lights no lanterns over the trench.
- **What people believe.** In Aetheris, some believe it leads to another world. [BELIEF, and true]
- **Tidecant.** Sailors mix Common and Kaelish into a pidgin called Tidecant. Smugglers move people across it. (A: Everyday life; A: Adventures anywhere)

sections.heading: Established nature
sections.content: The Bloom is a weather of minds in the mycelium, not a single speaking mind. It thinks by pulse and growth. Communion opens a person to it, at a cost in self; those who go too deep may cease to know where they end.

sections.heading: Practice and boundaries
sections.content: Spore-bound people listen through roots, read memories in old mycelia, grow living houses and heal with membranes that remember the body’s intended form. The membranes cannot take iron. Adaptive spores permit temporary passage through hostile Bloom. The Bloom drank Kaelith constructs and learned from them; circuit-roots and Arbors followed.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.content:
From east to west, the world runs:

1. [Aetheris](/player/e/CON-001)
2. The Eternal Veil's dusk coast
3. [The Black Tides](/player/e/LOC-902), a sunless sea
4. Kaelmar's east coast, with the port of [Kaelholm](/player/e/SET-302)
5. [Kaelmar](/player/e/CON-301)

The Rift runs beneath all of it, from the centre of Aetheris to the north-west of Kaelmar.

sections.heading: Established lore
sections.content:
| Age | What the cards say |
| --- | --- |
| Before the gods | There was Fire. The first flame still burns without fuel in [the Ashen Wastes](/player/e/LOC-004). Some call it creation's source, others what remains at the end. |
| The whole world | One world existed, unbroken and eternal. |
| The Shattering | The Elders broke the Ethereal Crystal. See COS-902. |
| The age of gods | Gods fought at the Titan's Fall, and their colossal skeletons still lie there. Their weapons were made at the Nameless Forge. One god tried to sit the Shattered Throne and failed. |
| The Cycle | Again and again a faction gathered the shards and remade the world. The Hidden Ones guided each turn and erased whoever came too close to the truth. |
| Things erased | A war nobody remembers: the Bloodless War. A king who tried to seize the Loom: the Unraveled King. A city stolen from the surface and sunk: the Drowned City. Someone who tried to break the Aetherfall and was unmade. |
| The Broken World | The last great kingdom fell. Its capital, Ashen Spire, is a ruin. The shards were lost again, and no faction holds power. |

sections.content: The Radiant Ascendancy is one of the five coexisting dominions of Aetheris Unbound. This is a region shaped by the faction named below, not a replacement timeline or a future Aetherfall.

sections.heading: Faction
sections.content: Celestial Order. Its faction page records doctrine, leaders, signature forces and political pressures.

sections.heading: Capital and chief fortress
sections.content: Empyrean Spire, a floating city of white stone. The High Theurgists rule from the Throne of Light. Chief fortress: the Golden Aerie.

sections.heading: Other sites
sections.content: The Radiant Expanse (golden plains), the Luminara Gate (an arch of light at the world's edge), the Purged Halls (a city erased for rebellion).

sections.heading: Rival enclaves
sections.content: Bastion of the Unbroken (Legion), Sanctum of the Everseeing (Consortium), the Eclipsed Chamber (Pact), the Thornward Grove (Wildborn). The Grove is New: an old grove on the edge of the Radiant Expanse, tolerated as a shrine to Solenne while its keepers quietly shelter Wildborn fleeing the Order.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.content: This is one material world with two continents: [Aetheris](/player/e/CON-001) in the east and [Kaelmar](/player/e/CON-301) in the west. [The Black Tides](/player/e/LOC-902), a sunless sea, separate them. Both shores touch the same Ethereal Realm, called *the between* in Kaelmar. The Rift is one wound whose two open ends meet through that realm.

sections.heading: Date at campaign start
sections.content: The shared present is **300 After Bloom (AB)** in Kaelmar, **Year 31 Unbound** in Aetheris. The calendar has 363 days: twelve 30-day months and three festival days outside the months. The gods, coinage and much of the language base are shared. See [Calendar](/player/e/SYS-901), [Money](/player/e/SYS-902), [Languages](/player/e/SYS-903) and The Gods.

sections.heading: How the continents meet
sections.content: The Black Tides crossing between [Kaelholm](/player/e/SET-302) and ports of [the Eternal Veil](/player/e/REG-005) takes about two weeks; regular ships have only recently begun to cross. The Rift also connects the continents through the Ethereal Realm's border layer. Root-roads in Kaelmar provide another approach to the border layer.

sections.heading: Aim
sections.content: Tools that work.

sections.heading: Methods and identity
sections.content: Ashvale's artisans, called Technologists in the novel. They make warding stones, listening bowls, walkers and grafted orchards.

sections.heading: Status at 300 AB
sections.content: Led by Chief Wright Brenna Halvor.

sections.heading: Associated people and places
sections.content: Brenna Halvor

sections.heading: Tensions
sections.content: They need usable salvage from the waygate while other factions fear waking old work.

sections.heading: Established description
sections.content: Seat of the Spore Circle’s Eastern Tendril, whose members burn Kaelith works and carry gourd-grown lamps.

sections.heading: Sea crossing
sections.content: Ships travel across [the Black Tides](/player/e/LOC-902) between [Kaelholm](/player/e/SET-302) and unnamed Eternal Veil ports. The passage takes **about two weeks**. Crew extinguish lanterns over the trench where the Rift runs below the sunless sea. Regular crossings are newly established by campaign start; smugglers also use the route.

sections.heading: Rift crossing [HOMEBREW]
sections.content: The Rift has an open end in the Hollow Marches and another by Ashvale. Travellers can enter one end, cross the Ethereal Realm's border layer, and emerge from the other. The source suggests this route for parties around level 11 and above.
